subject: Startups
title: Equity for International Employees
description: One-minute skill: Equity for International Employees.

hook.text: A US startup offers stock options to an engineer in Germany. The tax implications are fully different—and often worse.

buildup.text: Each country taxes equity differently. Some tax at grant, some at vest, some at exercise, and some at sale.

discovery.text: In some European countries, employees owe tax when options vest—even though they can't sell the shares yet. Cash trap.

twist.text: Employer of Record services like Deel and Remote help structure compliant equity for global teams. It's still complex.

climax.text: Ignoring international equity tax rules can create surprise bills—for employees and the company.

punchline.text: Equity across borders is a tax minefield. Walk carefully.

quiz.question: What's the challenge with offering equity to international employees?
options: Stock options don't work outside the US
Different countries tax equity at different stages
